cycle4.title: The IDP four-step cycle
cycle4.sub: One round a year. The ring is the IDP method; click a step to see its questions, then jump to the part of this page that answers each.

steps.name: Career intent
steps.sub: Where I want to go, who I want to become

method.q: Skills needed for the current (or future) role

steps.name: Self-assessment
steps.sub: Where I am now, who I am

method.q: Identify my main strengths and distinctive talents
Recognize areas to strengthen or improve (the competency gap)
Set development goals from career intent and self-assessment

steps.name: Plan
steps.sub: How to get there, how to grow

method.q: Turn development goals into concrete items (skills, knowledge or behaviour change)
Prioritize the items and plan timing and resources
Reach agreement with my manager and gain support
Review and track progress regularly (use the performance cycle's checkpoints to discuss with my manager)
Measure the effect and adjust in time

iceberg.title: The competency iceberg
iceberg.sub: Competency is more than the visible knowledge and skills; it includes attitude, values, traits and motives below the water. Click one to see where I stand.
iceberg.source: Spencer, L. M. & Spencer, S. M. (1993). Competency at Work.

items.name: Knowledge
items: MA in finance, quant research and an empirical thesis
The FSC's AI principles and pre-launch governance
How AI projects cost: GPUs, tokens, licences

items.name: Skill
items: Python, SQL, FastAPI, React: I build prototypes myself
Cost-benefit models, test design, acceptance question banks

items.name: Attitude
items: Curious about the business: I learn it without waiting for requests
Evidence first: data, not gut feeling
Launch is not the finish line: results get tracked after

items.name: Values
items: Accountable for value: every AI investment must say whether it was worth it
Pragmatic: I know when not to use AI

items.name: Traits
items: Problem framing: break vague problems into testable ones
Cross-disciplinary: I can talk finance, technology and governance

items.name: Motives
items: Take AI from pilots to real use
Challenge “we've always done it this way” and make the process better

blueprint.title: Three-year development blueprint
blueprint.sub: From proving value with the business to owning AI's results and investment

phases.name: Co-create value
phases.line: Use evidence to win the investment

tasks.d: Pick one AI agent scenario; confirm the business owner, baseline and target; map the current and future journey; write the business case

tasks.t: Pilot and pass the investment gate
tasks.d: Run an 8–12 week pilot in the real process, gather evidence and capability gaps, write the investment proposal, and lead business, IT and security to a decision

phases.milestone: At least 1 scenario with measurable pilot results; the first investment proposal done

phases.name: Build capability
phases.line: Turn investment into capability and results

tasks.d: Plan the data, API and system build, and move the AI agent from assisting to controlled action
Review adoption, cost and benefit monthly, and use the realization rate to scale up or adjust

phases.milestone: 1 customer journey changed; 2 consecutive periods of benefit tracking on target

phases.name: Own the value
phases.line: Own the value stream and its portfolio

tasks.d: Own one value stream and its investment portfolio, and chair the quarterly portfolio review
Turn cases and methods into a reusable team playbook, and coach new colleagues

phases.milestone: Own 1 reusable AI method or module; become a value owner

have.v: MA in finance, quant research, empirical thesis
RAG, multi-agent, MCP, VLM, LLM evaluation
Pre-launch checks, guardrail testing, cost-benefit framework

blueprint.goal: Turn business problems into AI solutions that are proven, investable and scalable, and own their results.
blueprint.tag: Finance × AI × value × collaboration | from finding the problem to scaling

goal: Within three years, move from turning processes into AI solutions to owning AI's results and investment.
tagline: Change how work gets done with AI first, then use evidence to win the investment.
scale: Can set the method for the organization

levels.name: Solution designer
levels.does: Turns processes into workable AI solutions

levels.name: Value co-creator
levels.does: Proves AI's value together with business units

levels.name: Value owner
levels.does: Owns AI's results and the investment portfolio

roadmap.title: Find a journey worth changing
plan: Pick one AI agent scenario and confirm the business owner
Set the baseline and the target
Map the current and future journey; write the benefit hypothesis

roadmap.title: Get evidence from a small pilot
plan: Inventory reusable platforms, data and APIs
Run an 8–12 week pilot in the real process, reviewed every two weeks
Track handling time, throughput and adoption

roadmap.title: The first investment gate
plan: Write the investment proposal: outcome, evidence, gaps, ask and return
Build the governance controls into the gate criteria
Lead business, IT and security to a stop, hold, invest or scale decision

roadmap.title: Turn investment into capability and results
plan: Plan the data, API and system build with IT
Move the AI agent from assisting to controlled action
Review adoption, cost and benefit monthly, for two periods in a row

roadmap.title: Become a value owner
plan: Own one value stream and its investment portfolio
Turn cases and methods into a reusable team playbook

measures.name: AI governance
measures.what: Assessment speed, control coverage, no major incidents

review: Results reviewed monthly, investment quarterly, and this plan updated yearly.
